scope: AirIndia / EGY full regression on ndc-supplier-integration: TestCases_Generic.csv + TestCases_V1.csv + TestCases_V2.csv + SeatMap_TestCases.csv + new AirIndia happy-scenario and exploratory rows
title_line: AirIndia / EGY - Full Regression - ndc-supplier-integration - V1 and V2 - 515 test cases
scope_text: Generic CSV (64 rows) + V1 CSV (59 rows) + V2 CSV (212 rows) + SeatMap CSV (68 rows), each executed or recorded BLOCKED with the reason, plus 117 new AirIndia/EGY rows (happy scenarios across passenger mixes, trip types, bundles, ancillaries and seats; request validation; ID-chain negatives; capability and security checks). Flows written for other suppliers are re-targeted to AirIndia/EGY; Hold, Void and Upselling flows are BLOCKED because AirIndia does not support them.
description_text: Full regression of the AirIndia supplier on the EGY credentials against https://ndc-supplier-integration.azurewebsites.net/ (a non-production host, booking authorized by the user), V1 and V2, with emphasis on happy scenarios and end-to-end flows. Inventory is available here, so every Family A flow (Search to Retrieve) is executed with real PNRs.

title: [Book][Request] Validate that submitting a second, different passengersSelectedSeats selection supersedes an earlier selection made earlier in the same test session (late seat-change-before-submission).
expected: Automatable assertion: Book succeeds and reflects cell B only -- passengersSelectedSeats/passengerSeats/totalSelectedSeats show cell B's cellCode/price; cell A does not appear anywhere in the response, and cell A's availability (per a follow-up GetSeatMap, if re-queryable) is unaffected by the abandoned selection.
actual: Not modelable on this API: a Book request carries exactly one seat per passenger and segment (an object keyed by segment); there is no seat-change step before Book, so "a second selection supersedes the first" cannot be exercised. The duplicate-key variant is covered by TC-BOOK-NEG-08.

expected: This case does not assert a pass/fail against the live API. It documents that: (a) User Story AC8's "securely authenticates with airline supplier APIs" describes THIS system's outbound credential handling toward suppliers -- a server-side/config concern, confirmable only via a backend credential-storage/config audit or the automation framework's own code review (PRD §7's Gap #1 already flags this as hardcoded tech debt), not via any request this Postman-collection-driven suite can send; (b) AC9's "provides logging" is confirmable only via log/observability review (PRD §7's ApiResponse logger, correlation-ID tracing), not via API response inspection. TC-SEATMAP-NEG-05 covers AC9's "handles errors gracefully" half, which IS API-observable.
actual: Not applicable to this run: the case tests the Postman collection / documentation or records a statement, not an API behaviour on AirIndia.

title: [SeatMap][Response] Verify GetSeatMap returns a structurally identical normalized response shape across suppliers using different native backend protocols.
spec_ref: SPEC.md §1.3, §2.7, §4.1, §4.7; User Story AC7 ("supports multiple airline Seat Map APIs and common protocols/formats")
expected: Automatable assertion: every supplier's GetSeatMap response conforms to the identical schema documented in SPEC.md §2.7 (same top-level keys, same seatMapDetails/cellDetails nesting) regardless of the supplier's native protocol -- differences are limited to data values (cellCode ranges, characteristics, pricing), never to the shape itself. A supplier whose response requires a materially different assertion path is a normalization defect in the supplier-adapter layer (§1.3), not an acceptable per-supplier variation.
actual: Out of scope: this run is limited to supplier AirIndia (credentials EGY); no call is sent to any other supplier. (the case names other suppliers or compares suppliers).
